How to Get Rid of Anxiety and Depression in Children and Adults?
Anxiety and depression are common in adults and children, and both diseases are treatable. The first line of treatment for adults is to use a combination of medication and psychotherapy. For children the first step is the use of a psychotherapeutic tool called cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT).
The most common anxiety and depressive disorders are related to stress in children and adults. These stressors can be physical or psychological. Physical stress is linked to obesity, diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Psychological stress can come from a variety of sources including home and school life, bullying, divorce, separation, grief or bereavement and illness. A person can suffer from both physical and psychological stress and the two can co-exist. Both stress responses are similar in that they can lead to depression and anxiety. However, while the physical response is associated with a loss of appetite, sleep and physical fatigue, the psychological response can cause insomnia, agitation, anxiety, restlessness and irritability. In addition, both stress response are associated, to a certain extent, with increased blood pressure. Therefore, it is common for people to suffer both anxiety or depression from the same stressor. People with depression have a greater tendency to experience both psychological and physiological stress. Thus, they are more likely to develop a physical as well as a psychological disease at the time of the stress reaction. If the depression or anxiety is severe enough, then it can even lead the person to suicide. This is because depression is more common than anxiety in people. It is also more severe. Depression is characterized by a lack of interest in daily activities and a persistent feeling of sadness and hopelessness. On the other hand, there is anxiety which is described by the feeling that a person is under stress or that things are going wrong. Anxiety is not always accompanied by depression. Instead, a common disorder in which both depression, depression-like symptoms and anxious symptoms occur is post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Doctor Answers (1) on What causes hand and foot skin to peel

Hi,
This is a common issue, and is most common in children. Peeling of the hands or feet is caused by the skin becoming dry, which causes the epidermis (the upper layer of skin) to be thinned and flake off. The normal response of this epiphyseal thinning is to re-epithelialize the surface of these areas, causing them to become dry and rough. This can be caused through a variety of causes, such as stress, dehydration, use of certain medications, or other skin conditions. If your son is using moisturizer, it could be a reaction to the moisturizing. However, if he is dry or dehydrated, this could also be the cause of his dry skin. For this reason, he may need to see a dermatologist for skin testing. In the mean time, you can help him by keeping his skin moisturized and preventing his nails from growing too long. You may also want to talk with him about his diet. Is he eating a balanced diet, with plenty of fruits and vegetables?
Best wishes, Dr. D December 15th, 2010

For example, you may want to go to a therapist and explore some of your feelings and experiences with them. Once you begin to feel better, it will be easier to deal with the outside world, but until then you need a safe place to talk to someone who is not only trained to listen, they are also trained in helping you feel comfortable with what you are feeling and giving you suggestions on how to cope. & Regards Doctor Answers 5 1 What is a bipolar disorder?
August 11th, 2010
{{ voteCount >= 0 ? '+' + (voteCount + 1) : ( votecount + 2) }}
Bipolar disorder is characterized by episodes of mood swings. Bipolar disorders are often accompanied by an increase or decrease in energy and a loss of interest in activities, and can be accompanied with a lack of concentration, restlessness, a change in sexual behavior, irritability, depression, or anxiety. The major symptoms associated with bipolar disorders include:
In the manic phase, the person may have increased energy, euphoria, anger, excitement, grandiosity, talkativeness, delusions, hallucinations, insomnia, sexual arousal, loss or gain of weight, suicidal thoughts, thoughts of death or suicide, an inability to sleep, impulsive behavior or self-injury, difficulty concentrating, lack or change of appetite, poor concentration and memory, decreased sex drive, feelings of being too energetic or too slow, social withdrawal, increased physical activity, excessive talking and behavior (e.g., running, gambling, shopping, etc.), and grandiose or unrealistic expectations.
The depressive phase is often characterized with feelings or thoughts such as depression or sadness, sleep disturbances, low energy level, feeling hopeless, hopelessness, guilt, worthlessness or hopeless thoughts and actions, sleeping too much or not enough, anxiety, trouble concentrating or remembering, unusual sexual thoughts or behaviors, inability or unwillingness to concentrate, appetite loss, weight loss (especially weight gain), unusual weight change, panic attacks, self harm, mood changes, changes in speech, speech changes or difficulty with speech. In a severe episode, there may be mood episodes lasting for several weeks. These episodes may include loss/gain of muscle tone, tremors, muscle stiffness, weakness, dizziness, palpitations, headaches, irregular heartbeat, seizures, confusion, abnormal thinking, agitation, paranoia, altered sense of smell, taste

What is Ovarian Hyperplasia?
July 14th, 2009
{{ voteCount >= 0 ? '+' + (voteCount + 1) : (votes = 1 ) }}
A lump is a benign tumor, typically benign. The lump could be ovarian hyperplastic or benign, but more likely benign if you are young and healthy. If you have a history of ovarian cancer or a family history, you should discuss the possibility of the lump being cancerous with your doctor.
If the doctor is not concerned about the size of your lump, it is likely to have no impact on your life. However, if your physician does have concerns, a biopsy will be done to determine its nature. A biopsied lump that is benign will need no treatment. On the other hand, an ovarian tumor that has not been biopied may require surgical treatment to remove the tumor and the surrounding tissue. In this situation, your oncologist may refer you to a surgical onco-surgeon. It is important to let your surgeon know that you may have been tested for ovarian tumors. This will help them to decide whether to perform surgery or not. Depending on the location of this lump (i.e., in the abdominal area), you could have surgery to treat the area. Surgery will not remove all of it, so you will continue to need treatment for the rest of that area for at least 3 years. As you get older, the risk of cancer may increase. Therefore, keep in touch with a gynecologist. Good luck!

What is thorbocupytopnia?
August 16th, 2011
{{ voteCount >= 0 ? '+' + (voteCount + 1) : (votes = 3) }}
Hello,
Thrombo-cupo-topnia is a rare auto-immune disease in which the immune system attacks platelets and blood vessels in the blood system. It is most common in patients with HIV, diabetes, or kidney disease. A number of treatments have been developed and can help in thoro-cupo topnia. The most commonly used is aspirin, which is used to reduce bleeding and improve platelet function. Other anti-platelet medications include fibrates (such as ticlopidine), which are given by injection, and aspirin (which is taken by mouth).
I recommend you see a rheumatologist who specializes in Autoimmune Diseases, such as Thrombus, Auto-Immune diseases, etc. He will be able to help you find the correct treatment for you. Good luck!
Dr. Robert B. Blumberg, MD Internal Medicine Physician New York Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell Medical Center Read More How to treat throbocep-tiopnia February 7th 2010 Dear Doctor, My son is diagnosed with throbocuppytenia. Is there any way to stop his threbocapy-tennia ?
Thanks Cynthia Hi Cynthia, throubocytopnenia is rare. There is not a specific treatment that can stop threboctopneia, but it can be controlled with medication. Aspirin is the most often used medication, however, other medications may also be prescribed. Most people do well on aspirin. If thirbocuppny is severe or the person has another disease, your doctor may prescribe a different medication that is more effective. Best wishes! Dr. James H. The bump is called the lingual papilla. It is the soft tissue that is between the teeth and the gum line. When the tooth is fully developed, the papillae are smaller and more visible. The lingua papillaryis is a thin, hard tissue which fills in the space that the tongue used to occupy.
A sore tongue and hearing loss may be associated with a toothless mouth. In this case, you may have a deviated septum or a cleft palate, which causes the hearing and pain to radiate to your tongue. If you can, speak with your dentist about your hearing. You can also schedule an appointment with an audiologist. A hearing test may reveal more about the cause of your symptoms. Your dentist should also be able to suggest a treatment plan that will help you to feel better and hear better. Good luck. Please note that you should not use aspirin, ibuprofen or acetaminophen in conjunction with oral pain medications, since they may aggravate the situation. They should be avoided for at least 24 hours before using them again, to give your body a chance to heal. Hope this helps!

I was just wondering if you could shed some light on this. My husband and I are both cancer survivors (me from lymphoma and him from colorectal cancer) and we are now trying to conceive a child. Our first attempt was a complete failure with a miscarriage and now we have been trying for a second time. We are not sure if it was the cancer or the treatments that caused the miscarriage. At this point, we want to start trying again but we don't know if that will make things worse or not. Any advice would be greatly appreciated. Thank you!
Thank you for your question. The fact that you are in complete remission is great news! It means that your cancer is under control and that it is very unlikely to return. Cancer is a very serious disease and it can be very difficult to treat, but you have made great progress and you should be proud of that. It is important to note that the risks of miscarriage increase with each successive pregnancy. If you and your husband have not had any previous miscarriages, this is probably not the cause of the problem. However, it would not be a bad idea to see a doctor to discuss the possibility of endometrial cancer and its association with pregnancy loss. You and he should discuss this with your doctor, who can make sure that both of you do not have other serious conditions that could be contributing to the loss of your baby. Please note, however, that there is no definitive link between endo and miscarriage, and doctors are still unsure as to why the two often go together. As always, you can visit the National Endometriosis Foundation website for more information about endomitosis. Good luck with the rest of this pregnancy!

I would suggest you see a dermatologist (a specialist in skin conditions) as they are best placed to advise you on this. Your doctor may have given you an oral anti-histamine, but this will have the effect of making the area worse, so you should only be given one if there is no other treatment option available. It is likely that your armband has become irritated due to sweating, as sweat can irritate the arm. This is more likely if you wear a sleeveless top or if your arm is exposed to hot temperatures. Sweat is also a common cause of skin rashes. If this is so, you may want to try wearing a sports bra or shirt with a neckline to prevent your shirt becoming damp and causing the problem. Alternatively, when you shower, try to avoid letting the water touch your arms and try and keep them dry. A good moisturiser is essential to help the inflammation and rash to go away. However, if the condition has not resolved after a while, or you find it difficult to deal with the symptoms, see your GP or dermatologists. They may be able to give you more appropriate advice and treatment options.

It is commonly associated with prematurity, malformed or missing feet, and sometimes with multiple congenitally defective feet. Overlapped toes affects only one foot and has no known cause. Sometimes, the toes overlap on one side of the foot, but not on both sides. In a few cases, two toes may overlap. The toes often overlap by a short distance (less than 1/2 inch) and can be affected by any of several factors: malformation of an external or internal malleolus or of a metatarsal, long bone, or a foot joint. These factors are the most common. A child born prematurely (before 37 weeks of gestation) with overlapping feet may have some degree of malformations, particularly in the feet or legs. An underdeveloped or defective foot may cause the overlapping foot to be more prominent than it should be.

text:
Q: What causes small holes in the outer ear?
A: This is a very common problem. The ear canal is surrounded by a thin membrane called the tympanic membrane that has a membrane over it to protect it from water and other things. This membrane is made of a tough substance called cartilage that is also called periosteum. In infants, cartilaginous tissue tends to harden with age. When this happens, it can break and tear, leading to small tears in this membrane. These tears can create small openings called holes or perforations in your tymnanic membranes. They can occur anywhere in a baby’s ear and are called tymmal perivascular lesions. Small holes are not dangerous, unless they are infected or cause a problem such as hearing loss or balance issues. However, there are times when tiny perovascular holes may develop into larger holes called choroid plexuses that lead to serious ear infections or hearing problems. To reduce the risk of infection, your child should wear a hearing aid. If your baby has small peruvian holes, he should have a fluid-filled tymphnomyectomy. A tymmyomyotomy is performed by inserting a long needle into your son‘s ears and draining excess fluid from the ear. Because the fluid is removed, small, fragile peruvascular membranes are preserved. Once the fluids are removed from your ear, you will notice that your ears are smaller. Your son will also have less fluid in his ears. Peruvian lesions are often treated successfully by placing ear plugs in one ear at a time. For more information, visit the American Academy of Otolaryngology at www.aao.org.

The virus can remain dormant for years, usually causing no symptoms in the majority of infected individuals. However, in approximately one out of every 100 individuals, the virus is activated and the infection progresses into cirrhosis and eventually liver cancer.
The HCV infection can cause damage to the liver and other organs, such as the spleen, pancreas, bile ducts, colon and intestines. In some cases, it can lead to liver failure and death. Infection with the HC virus has been associated with an increased risk for a number of other serious conditions, including:
 Heart disease It is important to remember that the risk of infection with HC V is greater in those with advanced liver disease. This procedure is usually done to look at the lining of the esophagus and the stomach. It's done under local anesthesia, so you're in no pain during the procedure. A gastroscopy is done the same way. The procedure involves inserting a thin tube called a scope into the body through your mouth or rectum. If you have lung or esphagitis, the doctor may also do an X-ray of your chest or abdomen. These procedures can help doctors diagnose the cause of symptoms. In addition, doctors can do a lung function test. They test the function of each lung and compare the results with lung scans to identify abnormalities. However, these tests are not always as accurate as they should be. Some people have very little lung damage and lung repair can be done later on in life. Lung repair is often done in children. Doctors may consider surgery, such as a thoracotomy, if you don't improve after a period of time. Surgery is considered if your symptoms are very severe and have been present for over a year. Please reply me as soon as possible,
A. HIV is transmitted through the exchange of bodily fluids, such as semen, vaginal fluids and blood. The chance of infection can be reduced if one of the partners is on treatment for HIV or has been in a monogamous relationship for at least one year. If the person is not on HIV treatment, the risk of exposure is very high.
The risk is higher if the infected person has a sexually transmitted disease (STDs). There are two types of STDS: Chlamydia trachomatis, gonorrhea, trichomoniasis, syphilis and genital warts. These STIs are often acquired during unprotected sex. Transmission of these STI can occur through sexual intercourse, oral sex, anal intercourse and sharing needles. Although they are not usually acquired from the same person, STD transmission can happen if an infected partner is in close contact with an uninfected partner. In this case, it is possible to transmit STIDs to an unaffected partner through skin-to-skin contact or by touching an object that has the STID on it. STTD can also occur if a person with HIV has unprotected oral or anal sexual contact, or is infected with both STIDS at the time of sexual activity. However, transmission of a STSTD can only occur when the infection is active. An infected individual with AIDS has no detectable infection. Therefore, an HIV-positive individual cannot transmit any STT to a non-infected person. There is also no evidence that HIV can pass from a mother to her baby during pregnancy. It is important to note that all STDI are curable. A person can cure or prevent HIV, if they take their medication.

Answer:Symptoms of Night Sweating A night sweat is usually a symptom of heat-related illnesses. It is the body's way of cooling itself. When you are sweating in your sleep, it is an indication that the heat is being absorbed into the blood stream. A night time sweat may be due to several factors. Most commonly, the sweating is due due the temperature of the air rising above your body as you sleep. Because of this, your skin absorbs the extra heat. This extra moisture can be uncomfortable. Another reason for night sweating may have to do with your diet. If you have certain types of food in you diet that cause your blood sugar level to drop, then this can also cause the skin to produce more sweat. Finally, a night of cold can cause you to sweat in order to maintain body temperature. Night sweats are not a cause for concern. They are usually just a way that your system is trying to regulate itself as your temperature drops. The more you sweat, and the more heat you absorb, you will become more comfortable.

Hi The mediASTYNUM is a small sac or pocket on your chest which is filled with fluid, air or fluid and air. It is very common, and is usually caused by a congenital lung defect. The mediasterynnus can be in the left or right chest, depending on where the defect is. If it's on right, then it would be on upper part of your left side. Usually, it can't be removed.
In a right mediasteynus, the fluid can come from the lung or the surrounding tissue. In a left mediastsyn, fluid may come through the sac, or from within the chest wall. If the area is red, tender, swollen, or sore, see your doctor for an examination. You will be given a prescription for cream to apply to reduce the redness, soreness and swelling. It can help to put a cold compress on it for about 10 minutes at a time. This should help, though it may take several days for the swelling to go down completely. A prescription medicine will also be prescribed. Do not use aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or ibuprofen (Motrin), as they can make the bruises worse. There is no cure for tuberculosis and there are no medicines which are 100% effective in treating tuberculosis. There are however some medications which may help reduce the severity of symptoms and the risk of further complications. This could be in the form of pills, injections or some other form. It is important to get a proper diagnosis of the disease and to find out which drugs might work best for you. The medications you are given will depend on your overall health, age, weight, and other risk factors. Your doctor will also need to know about your medical history, symptoms, family history and travel history. In most cases, the doctors will prescribe a combination of medications to help you fight the infection. These medications are generally oral and may be taken alone or in combination with other drugs. Some of these medications may require a prescription, so you should check with your doctor or the pharmacist. Once the diagnosis has taken place, you will be given information about the medication you may need. You will need a treatment plan which will help keep you healthy, prevent further infections and reduce your risk to tuberculosis in future. So, it is best to consult a doctor right away. For further information on tuberculosis, please visit the following website: 
In India, TB is mainly caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MtB), and is spread through the air by coughing, sneezing, or talking. TB can also be spread from person to person through blood, body fluids, food, water, etc. If left untreated, tuberculosis can lead to death and disability. According to a study published in Lancet, out of a total of 1.2 billion people who are living with tuberculosis around the world, India has the highest number of people affected by the illness. About 1,000 people die of tuberculosis every day. While it can be cured with proper medication, some people are left with long-term complications that require treatment. A person with active tuberculosis is at a higher risk for lung cancer, which is the second leading cause of cancer-related death

A. Glioma is a malignant tumor with a high risk of recurrence. The tumor cells may have spread to other parts of the body. Cancer cells are constantly dividing and dividing. When they divide, they can become cancer cells. This is called the process of cell division. At first, normal cells divide about once a day. They divide again about every 48 hours.
When cancer occurs, it is usually caused by a genetic mutation in one or more genes. These genes control the production of proteins that are essential for normal cell functioning. If a mutation occurs in the gene for the protein, then the cell must produce more of that protein than normal. In cancer patients, this leads to uncontrolled growth of cancerous cells and is known as cancer. There is no known cure for gliomacaloma. It may be possible to prolong the life of some people with glomacoma with chemotherapy and/or radiation therapy.

Penis pain and other erection-related problems are not uncommon in older men. In the early stages of erections, the spongy tissue surrounding the blood vessels that supply the corpus cavernosum (the part of your penis that fills with blood during an erection) becomes overly sensitive. This is referred to as an "oxidative stress" response. When the tissue becomes too sensitive, blood flow to the area can be blocked by blood clots, which can cause pain, swelling, and even permanent damage to tissue.
This is a common side effect of Viagra and Levitra and is sometimes called priapism. Priapus is Latin for "I will not quit." It is also called "the death penalty" or "a slow death." Priapsis is the most painful erection a man can have. As the body responds to an increase in blood pressure, it will attempt to expel the clog by pushing on the arteries. Unfortunately, this results in the erection becoming so large that it can't be retracted. If the blockage is not removed, an artery will eventually rupture and the man will die from blood loss. Men who suffer from priapsism must get emergency surgery to remove the clot. For most men, priapsesis only occurs once and can usually be controlled with a blood thinner. However, if priapse persists, surgery is required. Because priape is so painful and potentially life-threatening, doctors recommend that men who develop priapesis immediately stop using the drugs that caused it. (A note to doctors: Priape can happen to men of any age. Some doctors believe that priaped men are at higher risk for heart attacks and strokes.)

Heart palpiations are a common symptom and condition of the heart. They are generally caused by anxiety, stress, and/or physical stress. In some cases, heart palpitation is a symptom of a more serious underlying condition, such as an aneurysm or a heart attack. The cause of heart attacks is not always clear. Some people have a genetic predisposition, which predisposes them to heart problems, but the cause is still not known. However, there are some things that can help. Please see the next section to learn how you can make your heart conditions better.Heart palptations - CausesThe symptoms of palpations include one or more hard, strong, fast or irregular beats, sometimes accompanied by the feeling of pounding or fluttering in your chest. These symptoms can last from a couple of minutes to several hours. During heart beat, the muscles of your body contract and relax, often thousands of times per minute. There are many types of symptoms associated with heart beats. Many people experience symptoms such heart flutters, palps, pounding, racing, skipping, or palping. Palpitating symptoms are caused because the nerves in and around the chest and heart muscles are stimulated and sometimes abnormal electrical impulses travel along the nerve to the brain. When this happens, it causes the nervous system to send signals to your brain, causing you to have symptoms. Causes of PalpitationsA variety of conditions can cause palpatations. Anxiety, physical or mental stress (especially when you do not know what it is) and even a slight change in food or medication can affect your palpeptions. It is important that children have regular eye exams and that the pgygial and ocular systems are monitored closely. If the Pfie is diagnosed early, the child has a good chance of remaining in total remission without requiring any treatment. However, if the disease becomes more severe, treatment may be required. A patch is a type of dressing that is applied to the skin on the site of a wound or a cut. A patch may contain a liquid, a gel, or both. The patch can be used to cover a large area of skin or just a small area. It can also be applied directly to a site on a patient.
It is important to know that the patch does not change the nature of the wound. Instead, it is used for healing, prevention, and comfort. In most cases, the dressing is removed after the patient's wound heals. When a dressing remains on an injury, there is potential for infection and tissue damage. You may want to consider using a cream or ointment instead. These can help to prevent infection by preventing the fluid from the healing wound from getting into the bloodstream. Hi,
 AFB is acute flaccid paralysis of the respiratory tract. It is caused by a fungus called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The fungus is present in the lungs of most people but not in healthy adults. If you have been to a doctor and found out that you are not infected with tuberculosis, this is not the cause of your problem. Your doctor should have done a blood test and done an AFB test.
If you still have not been tested for tuberculosis and your doctor believes that this may be the problem, then your first step should be to get a second set of tests. This is called a bronchoalveolar lavage. A bronco-alive lavagge may show that there is still M tuberculosis in your body. There are several other causes of AFB. These include viral infections, bacterial infections and other fungal infections. See a new doctor. You need to rule out all possible causes first. We are more than happy to answer your questions. Thanks. Dr. S. P. Gupta Answered by: Dr S P Gupta, MD Certified Respiratory Therapist

text: A. Ichthyososis (also known as erythroderma), is an autosomal recessive skin condition that causes the skin to lose its pigmentation, especially in the face, hands and feet. This condition is caused by a defect in a protein called ilysin, which is found in some types of algae. It is a disorder of the body’s immune system, and causes damage to the cells lining the blood vessels. The skin becomes pale and the hands, feet and face become more sensitive and dry. Treatment is based on the severity of symptoms. In mild cases, cremes containing steroids may be used, or a simple diet may help to restore the normal skin colour. However, in more severe cases a combination of medications, such as steroids and vitamin E, may also be needed. Depending on how severe the ictyosis is, the treatment may require a round-the-clock care and may take years to completely cure. Most sufferers become very sensitive to sunlight, with many preferring to stay indoors. But others have no trouble with the sunlight and can go outside, as long as they use sunscreen. If a child has been diagnosed with ictsyososm, he or she should be seen by their doctor regularly. As the disease can be severe, they should take good care of themselves and take as many precautions as possible. Sunscreen is important, but they also need to be careful about the use of tanning beds, because they may make the condition worse. They should also avoid tanneries. Finally, if they spend a lot of time at the beach or in pools, then they must be very careful not to pick at their skin or get it wet.

Hello,
Yes, you can have a child with thyroid disease.
In the case of hypothyroidism, the ovaries are the only tissue that can produce eggs. Thyroids produce the hormones that regulate the menstrual cycle and ovulation. So the symptoms you have are related to the thyroid. If you feel that you are not ovulating, it may be due to hypo or hyperthyroid. Treatment for hypothryoidism is the same as that for hyperthroid, and both are reversible. Talk with your doctor about what treatment to recommend. Good luck!
If you really want to have more children, then you should consider having a hysterectomy. This is not a permanent solution, but it would eliminate the issue of menstrual cycles and your fertility. I know this is a very personal decision, so you will need to discuss it with a doctor. The benefits of a uterus are many, including the ability to carry a baby to term. All the best. :)

Psychosis is defined as a mental disorder that involves a persistent, disruptive pattern of thinking, feeling, or behaving that interferes with the ability to carry on a normal daily activities.
It is most commonly associated with hallucination and delusion. Hallucinations are visual images, sounds, voices, odors, etc. that can be perceived by the senses. Delusion is an incorrect belief about reality. People with psychosis experience both hallucinations and delusions. The hallucinogenic drugs, such as LSD or PCP, can increase the symptoms of psychosis. Psychosis can occur in people who are not on drugs. In some people, psychosis can also be caused by brain damage, illness, stress, and/or alcohol abuse. Severe psychosis is associated in some cases with suicidal behavior. If you or someone you know has been experiencing hallucinations or delusions, please call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

A. Abitrex is a type of anti-psychotic drug. Its main action is to inhibit the action of certain neurotransmitters and brain chemicals, which make us feel sleepy. This can result in daytime sleepiness, sometimes known as 'drowsiness'. This feeling is more likely to occur when you are taking the drug in larger doses or for a longer time.
In some people, the feeling of being tired is increased when they are also taking certain medications, such as antibiotics. If you have any concerns, it is always best to speak to your doctor.

Your partner probably had a number (or all) of these, so you should be able to get him off the strong antibiotics and see if the problem goes away. If it does, he probably just had an upset stomach. 3 years, 6 months ago TMD There are a few possibilities that you can rule out. The most common cause of swollen lymph nodes is a bacterial infection, such as cellulitis. Another is an allergic reaction to an ingredient in your child's medication, which is more likely in a child who is two years old. In addition, a virus can cause swelling.
If you suspect cellulite, you should see a dermatologist. They can perform a physical exam and examine your son's lymph glands for a possible infection. He may be prescribed medication to help reduce the swelling, as well as a cream to soothe and moisturize the area. You may also want to see if there is any pain that is associated with the swollen area, and if not, the doctor may recommend an ultrasound to check for abscesses or other fluid-filled cavities. If this is the case, your doctor can prescribe antibiotics to treat any infection that might be causing the problem. Finally, if a viral infection is ruled out, he may need to be seen by an ENT doctor to rule it out as an allergy. Although it's unlikely, it is possible that he has an ear infection or otitis media. These types of infections can also cause swollen glands. Lastly, an infection could be the cause for the fluid draining out of the lymph node, but it would be best to get him evaluated by a doctor who specializes in pediatric medicine. Good luck!

Doctor Answers 6 What is a benign brain tumor? June 24th, 2011
{{ voteCount >= 0 ? '+' + (voteCount + 1) : (votes = 0) }}
The lump you describe sounds like a meningioma, a brain tumor that is benign. A benign tumor is not cancerous,
and does not cause cancer.
A benign meningocele is the most common type of benign brain tumor. It is about two to three times more common than the next most commonly occurring benign type, the medulloblastoma. The meninge is usually very large, and can be painful. They can be detected by a neuropathologist with a specialized microscope. Sometimes, they can be detected through a CT scan. Often, this is done when the lump or bump has grown. If it has not grown, then there is no reason to be concerned. Meningiomas are not usually malignant, although it is possible for a tumor to grow into the meninges and cause a neurological or other problem. Occasionally, tumors will spread into surrounding areas, causing symptoms that are similar to meniere's disease or an infection. For example, sometimes a person can have headaches, dizziness, or vomiting, while having no other symptoms. These symptoms can go away without treatment, so the diagnosis does not need to come from a doctor. In most cases, it is simply a matter of waiting for it to go back to its normal size. You should be monitored, if you are concerned about the size of the tumor, by your doctor if there is any change in the growth or location of symptoms, for instance, increased pressure or pain. Good luck. Hope this helps. :)

A:
I would definitely call your doctor about this. I'm not a doctor, but I am a nurse practitioner. The first thing I would do is get the full list of lab tests done and get an MRI.
In the meantime, I'd tell you that this sounds like something else, like an arrhythmia. In an emergency situation, you should call 911, even if it is just an ambulance ride, and tell them that you have chest pains and you are having trouble breathing. That way, they know what to expect and will be able to give you the best possible care. If you call the doctor's office, the nurse will likely just tell your to take some aspirin and see if that helps. Here are a few signs of bluns affect:
-You tend to say things out loud before thinking about how it will be taken. A cardiologist, a cardiothoracic surgeon, or an interventional cardiology doctor will be best. They will use a combination of tests to find out what's wrong with you, so you'll need a list of questions to ask your doctor before you go. For example, the Echography will show if the heart muscle is getting stiff and the ECGs will check for any abnormal heart rhythms. Then, they will do a stress test to determine if your heart can handle stress. After that, if all is well, your doctors will probably recommend you keep doing what you're doing and see how it goes. However, it's always a good idea to be proactive and take precautions. You can do that by talking to your family doctor about your health and getting some advice on how to stay healthy. Thanks for this question! I'm Dr. Gopalan.
The answer to your question depends on how your blood is being tested. The first test is usually done with a stethoscope, and you would be asked to listen to the sounds that you hear in your chest. This would give your doctor a good idea about how well your lungs are working. A second test, called an echocardiogram, is performed in a hospital or doctor's office. While an EKG is a very common test in hospitals, it is not very useful for people who are taking medicine that affects blood flow. An Echochrone test may be more useful, but this test also requires a specialized clinic. It may also take a couple of weeks for your test results to come back. Since there is no guarantee that your ECH will be useful in the future, you should definitely not continue on your medicine if you do not need to. You should ask your prescribing doctor whether or not it would benefit you to have another test done to see how things are going. When you stop taking your medication, the blood vessels in and around your heart may become swollen. Your heart has to work harder to pump blood through the enlarged vessels, which can cause your symptoms to get worse. However, if your arteries have already started to narrow, a change in medicine may not be helpful. So, even though you may feel that continuing on the medication may help you, please do so only if it makes sense to you. Best of luck!

Answer:
Radiotherapy is a treatment for kidney stones. It involves using high-energy X-rays to destroy the stone. The treatment is quite effective, but it also involves risks to the patient.
First of all, radiotherapy can damage the kidneys. If the treatment damages the kidney, the renal function will be affected, and the person will not be able to urinate normally. There is no way to determine whether the radiotherapist has damaged the body. Secondly, there is also the risk of cancer development in the treated area. This risk is not very high, because the X rays are very low energy. But, it is still a risk. Moreover, when the radiation dose is very large, a part of the healthy cells of other organs can be damaged. These cells are known as radiation-sensitive cells, or radiation induced cells. They will never recover from the damage. So, they will have to be treated in order to prevent cancer. Thirdly, if the organ that is being treated has a weak blood supply, then it will become enlarged. That means the cancer will spread to other parts of your body, such as the liver or lungs. To prevent this, you should make sure the area that will receive the high radiation dosage is protected by a strong blood vessel. In particular, to protect the brain, an operation to insert an arteriovenous graft (AVG) is necessary. An AVG is an artificial blood flow that can carry blood from one part to another. When a person has an AVH, he or she can have an enlarged brain. Therefore, in addition to avoiding radiating areas with weak vessels, radiation protection is needed for the whole body to avoid this problem.

A. Snake bites, especially if they are of the venomous variety, are a rare phenomenon. However, it is not unusual for the patient to develop some swelling of localised sites after the administration of anticoagulants and other medications. It is usually the swelling that is the most distressing symptom, as it can be a nuisance and be distracting. There is no known remedy for this condition. Once you have treated the bite, you can try to keep the area moist and dry by using a warm compress or a moistened cloth and avoid using perfumed creams, perfumes or lotions, which can aggravate the symptoms. You can also try applying cold compresses, in which you put a few drops of oil or cream and wrap the compress around the bitten area for a couple of minutes. This will help to ease the itching and swelling. A few ice cubes can help soothe the temperature. Keep the wound clean and covered with a clean gauze bandage, and give the affected area ample time to heal.

It is considered to be a localized inflammation of the skin that is characterized by redness, scaling, pain, itching, inflammation, heat, red marks, swelling, tenderness or tender points. While cellulites can occur on the legs of men and women alike, they are more common in women.  Infection (fungal or fungeal)
o Diabetic foot ulcers b Injuries c Trauma d Inactivity e Alcohol abuse f Cancer g Other skin conditions, such as psoriasis, eczema, rosacea or acne, may also be associated with cellulitics. There are many possible causes for weakness or pain as you describe. You should consult a physician to determine the cause.
The most common cause of weakness and pain that is not considered a medical emergency is a nerve infection. This type of pain can be caused by a variety of different viruses, bacteria or other infections. They can affect the nerves in your arms, legs, buttocks, or even your spine. If you have a fever, pain, tingling, numbness, weakness, stiffness or swelling in any part of your body, especially your lower body (especially your legs), you should see your doctor. A nerve condition called transverse myelitis is the most frequent cause, but many other causes of nerve pain exist, including tendinitis, rheumatoid arthritis, lumbar disc disease, and a number of other conditions. Dear Vicki,
A period is when the uterus releases the uterine lining, or womb lining. This is a regular, monthly release of the lining from the womb, which is made of cells called mucus. When a woman is ovulating, the egg releases from within the ovary. The lining of this ovum is then released through the cervix and into the vagina, where it forms the period. A woman who has not conceived after a year or more of trying is said to have a "defect in ovulatory function", and may need fertility treatment to try again. If your periods are heavy or irregular, this may be a cause for concern. However, a medical check-up may reveal that you are fine. You can find out more about your menstrual cycle here: www.webmd.com/menstruations It's important to note that menopause is not the same as mengitis. Menopausa is the medical term for the condition, while menengitis is an inflammation of one or both of your ovaries. In some cases, menyopaulosis is also present. It is caused by a build- up of bacteria on the wall of a duct that leads to the fallopian tubes. Once the bacteria reaches the tubes, it can become trapped, leading to inflammation and inflammation-induced cancer. There are some symptoms of both mennopulsa and menngitis, including:

I am currently pregnant with my third child. I was diagnosed with gestational diabetes 3 months ago. My OB told me that I would have to be on insulin during my pregnancy. He is the only doctor I have ever seen that has suggested this. Is this a good idea? I had gestative diabetes with both of the other two pregnancies, and was able to control it with diet and exercise, so I don’t want to feel like I am going to have an insulin dependent pregnancy this time around. Also, I read that some people are not able control their diabetes when they are pregnant, due to the hormones. So, is it worth taking the insulin? What can I do to make sure that this is not the case? My first pregnancy I controlled my diabetes using a metformin tablet, which I took at night, in addition to my regular medication.
Thank you so much in advance!
Beth Dear Beth,
Gestational Diabetes occurs when a woman with diabetes is pregnant. The baby is born with this condition. If the mother is taking insulin, she can control the diabetes. However, if the woman is only taking a type 1 diabetes medication, then this cannot be done. There is no cure for gestural diabetes, the baby can only be treated with insulin. Insulin is a hormone that the body makes to convert sugar in the blood into energy. This hormone helps to keep blood sugar levels normal. In the majority of cases, a pregnant woman will need to take insulin to help control her diabetes during pregnancy and after the birth of her baby. Some people have been able or unable to properly control gestional diabetes in pregnancy, however this has been rare. Most women with diabetic conditions can manage their condition by following a healthy diet, exercising and taking their medication as directed. Many of these women have found that a diet low in sugar, high in protein and low glycemic index helps. A diet with these guidelines can help to reduce the risk of gestitional diabetes and reduce complications of pregnancy such as hypertension, pre-eclampsia and gestating diabetes mellitus.

Guillan-barre syndrome (GBS) is an autoimmune disorder caused by an antibody attack on the myelin sheath, which surrounds the nerve cells in the central nervous system. Nerve sheaths are made of a protein called myelination. When the immune system attacks this protein, the sheathing is destroyed and nerve function is lost. There are two types of GBS: primary and secondary. Primary GRS is usually caused when the body's immune cells attack the nerves of specific organs, such as the heart or the kidneys. Secondary GSR is caused from an infection of any type of bacteria or virus. GBM is the most severe type and is found in about 1% of people who have GCS. It causes a loss of muscle tone and weakness

White blood cell count
A white cell or WBC count is an indicator of the ability of a blood sample to detect white cells.
If the white count exceeds the normal range, it means the body is producing too many white cells. If it is below the range it indicates that the number of whitecells is too low. White cells are important because they are involved in the immune system. The body produces whiteblood cells to protect the tissues against infections. When the blood counts are high, the immune system is active. It is important that you ask your doctor about this. In addition, you should ask about other possible causes for your child's symptoms, such as a virus or bacteria.

text: ASO is a measurement of the blood levels of certain substances that are produced by the liver. These substances are present in the bloodstream in small amounts. When these substances accumulate in high amounts, they can cause health problems. The liver produces certain chemicals that can build up in your blood and cause problems, but the amount of these chemicals in you blood is determined by a number of factors. A small amount can be normal, and a large amount could be an indication of liver problems or other health issues. For example, a person with liver failure may have an elevated ASOL. Another example is the presence of elevated levels in patients with cirrhosis of The Liver.The liver is responsible for filtering and removing dangerous substances from your body. It is also responsible, in part, for producing certain hormones. Your liver may be functioning improperly, which may affect your hormones and make it difficult for your organs to function properly. Symptoms of this condition may include:Nausea and vomitingDiarrheaFeverWeight lossFatigue The symptoms may appear suddenly or gradually. Some people who have liver disease may not experience any symptoms at all. If you think you may suffer from liver disorders or liver dysfunction, you should consult your physician. In addition, liver function tests may need to be performed to determine the cause of your symptoms.

avies Doctor Answers (2) on How can pneumonia and sepsism be treated
Dr.
K.J. Sharma
(Dr Sharma is the Director of Clinical Research,
Paediatric and Adult Respiratory at the Royal Brompton Hospital)
August 26th, 2012 This is a very complicated question. It depends on the cause of the pneumonia and septicemia. However, both of these conditions can be managed and the chances of a cure are high if the underlying causes are addressed. Pneumonia is a bacterial infection which is caused by bacteria called Streptococcus pneumoniae or pneumococci. The bacteria are spread through airborne particles and are inhaled by the nose. These microorganisms can also be found in the mouth and lungs when the patient is in hospital and may have been infected by an airborne virus. In this case, the bacteria in the lungs can cause pneumonia. Severe pneumonia can be life threatening and is associated with a high risk of death. Fortunately, pneumonia is now manageable with antibiotics and supportive care. If pneumonitis is secondary to an infectious process (i.e. septicaemia), the first step in treatment is to isolate the source of infection by testing for Strepsilococcal bacteria. This is done by taking a swab from the throat area. Depending on whether the result is positive for Streptococcic or not, antibiotics may be prescribed or a course of intravenous antibiotics could be started. Both the bacterial and viral causes of pneumonia are highly infectious. Therefore, it is essential to immediately isolate and test the person for the presence either of bacteria or virus if they are suspected to be the causative agent. Early diagnosis is important as this can help in reducing the risk of complications. More information can always be obtained from your local medical centre

The reason for this is because we have grown up with a society that is obsessed with perfection and success, both of which are based on perfection. Thanks Hi,I am a 32 year old woman with PCOS and Polycystic Ovary Syndrome. I was diagnosed with polycystitis oviductis in 2004 and have been on oral contraceptives since. In the past year, my polyps have increased and I have a lot of cysts. My doctor wants me to stop taking the pill and start taking a vaginal ring. Is there a risk of pregnancy?
Do you have any advice?Thanks Maria Answer: You should use contraception regardless of whether you are on birth control or not. The contraceptive pill contains estrogen, which can increase the risk for polyp growth. When taking birth-control pills, this risk is even higher for women with Poly-cysted ovaries.
When taking hormonal birth controls, the estrogen in the pills can affect your ovulation. Polyp development can be influenced by the hormone levels in your body. This is why your doctor has suggested that you stop using oral contraception. It is important to note that this does not mean that if you were to become pregnant, you would not get pregnant. If you plan on becoming pregnant and are taking oral contraceptive pills without a break, it is highly recommended that your physician evaluate your condition to see if there is a better method of contraception that could be used. You may consider a combination birth and contraceptive method that would reduce your risk. A combination method is one that contains both birthcontrol and a hormonal method such as a ring or patch that prevents ovulations. There are also some methods that can delay ovulatory cycles in order to reduce the amount of estrogen present in a woman's body when she ovulates. These methods include progestin-only birthcontrollers and levonorgestrel- only birth controlling methods.

These are probably keratosis pilaris (also known as KP). KP is a type of benign skin condition that can be caused by excessive exposure to the sun, by skin disease, or by certain medications. Some people get it in clusters on their palms and soles or on the backs of their hands. It can also appear on other parts of your body.
KP can look like small red bumps, a rash, moles, warts, pimples, limes, and other skin lesions. However, in most cases, it's just an overgrowth of skin cells that causes the bumps and luster. To help with the itching, you can use over-the-counter anti-itch creams. If the condition is severe, dermatologists may prescribe medicine to help reduce the amount of new skin growth.

Yes, it is normal for some people to experience the taste and smell of toothpastes after they rinse them out, as you have experienced. Some people may also experience other symptoms such as a sore throat or a metallic taste. These symptoms may be due to a bacterial infection that can develop in a toothbrush or tooth paste. Bacterial infections in toothbrushes and tooth pastes can result in oral health problems. If you experience these symptoms and you do not have a dental problem, you should see your doctor. An infection in teeth can lead to tooth loss and gum disease. You may want to contact your dentist about an appointment to determine whether or not your symptoms are due your tooth brush or if you need to see a dentist. However, if your condition is related to bacteria, your treatment may involve a prescription tooth rinse. The pain you are describing is most likely due to your heart's natural response to a heart attack. This is an acute response that occurs within minutes to hours of a coronary artery occlusion. As the heart is working to pump blood, it is also working hard to push blood through the small blood vessels that feed the lungs and to other vital organs.
Once the blood has been pumped through these vessels, the body begins to recover. Heart muscle begins rebuilding and the veins and arteries begin to dilate. A:
You may be wondering how to answer this question. However, a condom doesn't have to be 100 percent effective to protect you from pregnancy. What that means is that if you were to have sex and the condom breaks, you can still be protected from a pregnancy that could occur if the penis is not 100-percent erect. For this reason, we recommend that you wear a contraceptive method, such as a latex condom or an implant, during sexual activity. You should also be aware that the sperm in the semen can travel through a hole in a broken condom, making it possible for a sperm to reach your uterus. If you have a sexually transmitted disease (STD), such a Herpes or HIV, and you are not currently using a treatment, then you may also have an increased risk of getting pregnant. Also, if your partner is having sex with someone else, the possibility of transmission is even greater. These are just a few of the possible ways that unprotected sex can affect your pregnancy status. It's important to know that pregnancy can occur even if a person is wearing a barrier method. In fact, pregnancy is more likely to occur when a woman is using the barrier methods and her partner has an STD. When you consider the different types of contraception available, it's clear that there is a wide variety of methods that can help protect your health. Your doctor can provide you with specific information about the most effective method for you. We hope that this information helps you to understand the risks and benefits of having unprotected sexual intercourse.

T A: Anxiety Disorder is a very common disorder, and there are many types of Anxiety. Panic Attacks are typically triggered by a specific event, such as a stressful situation, that sends a message to your body that it is under threat. The brain responds to these messages by releasing the stress hormone cortisol, causing your heart rate to increase and your blood pressure to rise. This causes a feeling of panic that can last from a few seconds to several minutes. In some cases, the panic can trigger a full-blown panic episode, in which you feel like you are having a heart attack or losing your mind. These episodes can sometimes occur several times a week. You may also experience a sense of dread, fear, or hopelessness during your episodes. A. Diarrhea is the most common reason for flatulence. Flatulence is a gas that is released from the rectum and the upper part of the large intestine. The gas is usually produced by the bacteria in the intestines. It may also be caused by an imbalance in nutrients and minerals in your body. If you have diarrhea, then you may have gas. This gas may be produced and released on a daily basis. Gas can also come from an excess of certain foods or a lack of minerals and vitamins in one's body and food. Certain medications can cause flatulent symptoms as well. These symptoms can be very annoying for your daughter and can interfere with her quality of life. There are several ways to treat flatulences and relieve your child's discomfort. Your doctor may prescribe a medication to control the gas, but it is important to give your doctor as much information as possible. Some of your questions may not be easy to answer. To better help you, here is some information about your condition:
Clostridium difficile infections (C. diff.) are caused when bacteria enter the small intestine and multiply. When they multiply, they release toxins into the body that can lead to diarrhea and abdominal pain. You should speak with your primary care doctor about the symptoms of a C. Diff. infection. Coughing, nausea and vomiting may occur. Treatment for C diff is generally oral antibiotics. Since it can take up to 2 weeks for the medication to work, it may take several days to have a positive effect. Once the infection is treated, your symptoms should improve. But in some cases, C Diff can recur. In this case, the doctor will prescribe another course of antibiotics to try to cure the original infection and prevent recurrence.

A. Death is inevitable. It's also necessary. We all die. And when we die, we leave behind a lot of sorrow and pain. But fear is a natural response to death, and it's not unusual to have it. The best way to control fear about death is to talk about our fears. So, the first thing you need to do is talk to someone who you trust about your fears about dying. This person can be your family, a doctor or other health professional, or a friend. Tell this person about the feelings you have about how you are going to die and how worried you feel. Talking about these feelings is the key to getting rid the fears, because fear comes from a lack of understanding. For example, when you say, "I have a feeling that I'm going die," you're not saying that you know that's true. You're saying you don't understand why you believe that to be true and that it makes you worry. When you understand the reason that your fear exists, you can get a clearer picture of what you should do about that fear. Once you've talked to the person who will help you deal with your death fears and you get clarity about why your feelings exist, then you'll be better able to deal. Remember, if you talk, talk. Don't try to avoid talking about what's on your mind. That just makes the problem worse.

Back pain, especially a severe one, can be caused by a number of things. The most common cause of severe back and neck pain is a spinal herniation, which causes pressure to build up in the spinal column and can lead to pressure in other parts of the body. This can occur in either the lumbar or sacrum regions, depending on where the hernia is located. A spinal disc hernieiation is the most likely cause for severe pain in your lower back. In your case, the pressure on your spinal cord could have been caused either by disc bulging or a tear, but that's only one possibility. You should see a doctor to rule out any other causes. It's also possible that you have an inflamed disc. That's a possibility only if the disc is painful and swollen. If it's not painful, it may be inflating and is not a cause to worry about. Hope this helps!

text: A. Pimples are red bumps that appear on a surface and usually occur in clusters. They may be raised, flat, or lumpy, and may last for a few days or weeks. The term “pimple” is often used to refer to any red bump or lesion that is not a skin rash. A pimple may develop from an injury or infection, but most commonly it is a result of a hormonal imbalance. When the hormonal balance is out of whack, the body produces excessive amounts of oil and acne-causing bacteria, which can lead to the formation of pimples. Acne occurs in both boys and girls, although it tends to be more common in girls. Children’s skin is more prone to acne because it does not have the mature skin barrier that protects the skin of adults. As a teen, you may have heard of hormonal acne. This is acne that develops during puberty, often starting in the cheeks and forehead and spreading down the back of the face. Your skin can also develop acne if you have a family history of acne or if your acne is caused by a virus or bacteria. Some people also experience acne in their teens and early 20s, including those with a genetic predisposition to develop the condition. Hormonal acne usually clears up by age 18, except in those who have hormonal imbalances that do not clear up. If your pimply skin does persist, talk to your doctor. She or he can help you with your diagnosis and treatment. You may also be given a prescription medication that can reduce the frequency of your flare-ups.

Doctor Answers 2 Endometriosis is a condition in which endo tissue grows outside the uterus. The lining of the womb (endometrium) is normally shed each month during menstruation. Endometria that grow outside of your uterus can cause pelvic pain, infertility, chronic pelvic infections, ectopic pregnancy, severe pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) and endocervical cancer.

If endoplasmic reticulum (ER) tissue is found, the ER can be removed. Laproscopy can also be used to remove endomechia (the tissue lining your cervix) if you have had a previous endovaginal delivery or an ectocapsular pregnancy. In the future, if endomes are found to be the reason for your symptoms, you might need surgery to repair the damaged tissue or to insert a prosthesis. Doctor Answers 8 What is AFB?
October 19th, 2012
{{ voteCount >= 0 ? '+' + (voteCount + 1) : (votesCount+1) }}
Hi,
 AFB is acute flaccid paralysis of the respiratory tract. It is caused by a fungus called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The fungus is present in the lungs of most people but not in healthy adults. If you have been to a doctor and found out that you are not infected with tuberculosis, this is not the cause of your problem. Your doctor should have done a blood test and done an AFB test.
If you still have not been tested for tuberculosis and your doctor believes that this may be the problem, then your first step should be to get a second set of tests. This is called a bronchoalveolar lavage. A bronco-alive lavagge may show that there is still M tuberculosis in your body. There are several other causes of AFB. These include viral infections, bacterial infections and other fungal infections. See a new doctor. You need to rule out all possible causes first. We are more than happy to answer your questions. Thanks. Dr. S. P. Gupta Answered by: Dr S P Gupta, MD Certified Respiratory Therapist

Exercise induced fatigue is a symptom of physical or mental exhaustion that occurs after a session of moderate or vigorous exercise. It is also known as exercise induced hypertension, exercise intolerance, or exercise stress syndrome. Exercise is one of those things that most people do on a daily basis. Whether it’s running, swimming, biking, running in place, hiking, weight lifting, boxing, yoga, walking, playing sports, etc. it can all take a toll on your body. Your body‘s natural response to physical activity is to build muscle and burn fat. When you exercise your heart and lungs have to work harder to pump blood through the body, leading to fatigue. This is where exercise can become a problem. During exercise the heart beats faster and the lungs need to breathe harder. What is the treatment for shoulder pain?I have had shoulder problems for years, but now I have pain that I can t stand. I m not sure what it s from, so I am looking for some relief. What can I do?
Sarita, New York Hi,
There s lots of shoulder symptoms and pains, some of which can be very annoying. The muscles in the shoulder are very important, as they support the head and arm of the body. If the muscles are weak, they can cause shoulder pains. You ll find that many people have problems with shoulder aches, which is one of these. So, what can you do about this? There are lots and lots if treatments and exercises that can help you, including massages. But, the most important thing that you can try to do is to relax your shoulders. Try to let go of your tension and focus on your breathing. This will help to reduce your shoulder and muscle pain. Also, try not to carry much weight in your arms, or to lift heavy objects. These can really aggravate your problems. And if you have a lot of pain, you should go to a doctor and have your muscles examined. That s really the only way to know for sure if something is wrong. Good luck!
